gen-gf-noto-serif-np-hmong-fs-supreme: Literary and tall, with bowls that thin gently. Supreme sits underneath as a plain sans, heavy-looking and held open, and that weight against the heading's restraint is what makes the pair.
gen-gf-noto-serif-np-hmong-general-sans: General Sans draws each letter with steady pressure and an x-height that fills the line. Noto Serif NP Hmong sits above it, its tall lowercase and mild bar variation giving a sans body something to lean against.
gen-gf-noto-serif-np-hmong-manrope: Tall, bookish letters with a gentle swing. Manrope's bright open curves and single-width line keep a long stretch of text moving smoothly, while Noto Serif NP Hmong adds a quiet editorial tone.
gen-gf-noto-serif-np-hmong-montserrat: Noto Serif NP Hmong gives a mellow, literary swing in tall lowercase, while Montserrat glides beneath it like bent wire. Its wide counters make the reading feel easy.
gen-gf-noto-serif-np-hmong-switzer: Switzer is wire-like and tubular, with a tall waist line and tips that stay well apart. Noto Serif NP Hmong adds thins that never turn spindly, so the serif heading holds firm above it.
gen-gf-noto-serif-np-hmong-work-sans: Work Sans reads modern, with a marker-like line and a high mean line. Noto Serif NP Hmong does its best work in quiet stroke modulation and tall forms, while Work Sans simply keeps its line constant.
gen-gf-noto-serif-old-uyghur-archivo: Authoritative serif letters with a deep middle band meet a body whose curves open outward instead of curling in. Archivo's commanding x-height steadies the page.
gen-gf-noto-serif-old-uyghur-fs-asap: Asap reads openly, its c forms like arcs and its lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals. Noto Serif Old Uyghur adds a faint swell in each curve, so a long passage feels measured and sturdy.
gen-gf-noto-serif-old-uyghur-fs-epilogue: Curvy, loose and wire-thin below, deep-banded above. Noto Serif Old Uyghur earns its keep when set big and short, with Epilogue's plain sans lowercase and stubby ascender tips staying out of its way.
gen-gf-noto-serif-old-uyghur-fs-fira-san: Fira Sans reads large and open, with no thick and thin at all. Against Noto Serif Old Uyghur, whose thinnest strokes stay sturdy, the pair's strongest quality is how plainly the two roles divide.
